chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I stand [for night prayer] while fearing the dawn [has arrived].' He said, 'Then offer the Witr [prayer].' I said, 'Then I look [to see if it is still night], and if night is upon me.' He said, 'Then pray the night prayer.'

key_terms.أَوْتَر: To offer Witr, the odd-numbered prayer concluding the night prayer
key_terms.الْفَجْر: Dawn, the time for Fajr prayer

ai.seo_question: How should one perform night prayer if unsure whether dawn has arrived?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of night prayer (Salat al-Layl) in cases of temporal uncertainty, distinguishing between the obligatory Witr and the voluntary night prayers based on the presence of darkness. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of relying on the prevailing state (istishab) of night until clear evidence of dawn appears, ensuring the continuity of worship. This guidance underscores the flexibility and depth of night devotion in Shia tradition, where the distinction between Witr and Tahajjud is maintained even during the transition period before Fajr.
